To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the land-use intensity of a given landscape is the main driver of the number of ecosystem services provided by the landscape, (ii) land-use intensity is positively associated with the number of ecosystem service types provided by the landscape and (iii) the number of ecosystem functions that are performed by a given landscape increases with land-use intensity.

(1) there is a need for a more holistic approach to land-use planning and management in order to achieve sustainable land-use planning and (2) the current land-use planning and land-use policy in the Netherlands are insufficient to achieve the goal of sustainable land-use planning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of ecosystem services in the development of land use and land cover, as well as the implications of these changes on the ecosystem services themselves.
the evaluation of the effects of land use change on ecosystem services.
the evaluation of ecosystem services in a landscape context and the impact of land-use change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
land use changes are a major threat to the biodiversity in the world and that the loss of biodiversity has negative consequences for ecosystem services.
the human impact on the environment is both positive and negative, but the negative impacts outweigh the positive ones.
the human activities have a significant impact on the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that land use change and ecosystem services are strongly interlinked, and that land use change is the main driver of ecosystem service provision and change, and that ecosystem service provision can be used to inform land use change.
we are not able to predict how the future will look, but we can provide a framework for the future, and a set of scenarios that are likely to be the future.
we need to develop more effective methods for the assessment of ecosystem services, and that we need to integrate the assessment of ecosystem service change with the assessment of land-use change.

the ecosystem services of a landscape can change dramatically over time.
